Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Diagnosis accesses the item embedding table through `item_emb.weight` and sequence representations through `log2feats(sequence)`. Model internals are not supplied, so the encoder architecture and representation computation cannot be established. The probe uses features for every sequence position; it does not explicitly extract a final user representation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(model, device)` stores the supplied model or compatibility view, plus its `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. Only metadata is subsequently queried; reviews and stored histories are unused.

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` invokes two probes. Training batches supply `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with shape `B × L`. Sequences are converted to NumPy before `log2feats`; positive and negative IDs are stacked into `B × L × 2` candidates for `predict_score(features, items)`. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`:** Samples up to 2,048 nonpadding item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal pairwise cosine similarities, and maps the mean to `[0,1]`. Higher values suggest directional collapse; approximately 0.5 corresponds to near-zero average cosine.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`:** Mean and lower tenth-percentile positive-minus-negative score across up to ten batches. Higher values indicate stronger separation, including difficult positions.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`:** Fraction of margins below zero; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`:** Fraction of margins below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`:** Counts category occurrences separately for positive and negative items in low-margin and wrong-ranking cases, retaining the top 20 categories.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, input perturbation, or sensitivity tests occur. Negative candidates come directly from the loader. Margin evaluation disables gradients and sets evaluation mode without restoring the previous mode.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The returned dictionary contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both into instructions requesting a downstream JSON interpretation with status, findings, implications, and evidence.

These probes assess embedding geometry and sampled training-pair separation, not validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, or causal sequence sensitivity. Margins depend on score scale and negative sampling. Empty observations yield zeros that can appear healthy. Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so category lists remain empty; no category information should be invented.

Recent work cautions against equating ranking accuracy with useful order modeling. [Oh and Cho (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) propose measuring excessive recency emphasis and report improvements from mitigating it. [Liu et al. [Petrov et al. Their results distinguish benefits from earlier history, recency weighting, and joint contextualization; strong scores alone do not establish higher-order sequence use.

A practical diagnostic design suggested by these findings: freeze the trained model and candidate set; remove recent interactions, repeated occurrences, or explicitly defined isolated events; compare each intervention with equal-size random removals, additionally matching position or popularity where feasible. Popularity-only, last-item, and recency-weighted pairwise controls help separate sequence dependence from simpler signals. Connect observed sensitivity to positional embeddings, attention, and next-item supervision through controlled component ablations or retraining; prediction perturbations alone cannot identify which component learned the behavior. Removal effects assess model dependence and explanation faithfulness, but padding changes, position shifts, and implausible histories can confound them. These are computational interventions, not evidence of real-world causal effects on user preferences.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Diagnosis accesses the item embedding table through `item_emb.weight` and sequence representations through `log2feats(sequence)`. Model internals are not supplied, so the encoder architecture and representation computation cannot be established. The probe uses features for every sequence position; it does not explicitly extract a final user representation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(model, device)` stores the supplied model or compatibility view, plus its `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. Only metadata is subsequently queried; reviews and stored histories are unused.

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` invokes two probes. Training batches supply `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with shape `B × L`. Sequences are converted to NumPy before `log2feats`; positive and negative IDs are stacked into `B × L × 2` candidates for `predict_score(features, items)`. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`:** Samples up to 2,048 nonpadding item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal pairwise cosine similarities, and maps the mean to `[0,1]`. Higher values suggest directional collapse; approximately 0.5 corresponds to near-zero average cosine.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`:** Mean and lower tenth-percentile positive-minus-negative score across up to ten batches. Higher values indicate stronger separation, including difficult positions.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`:** Fraction of margins below zero; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`:** Fraction of margins below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`:** Counts category occurrences separately for positive and negative items in low-margin and wrong-ranking cases, retaining the top 20 categories.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, input perturbation, or sensitivity tests occur. Negative candidates come directly from the loader. Margin evaluation disables gradients and sets evaluation mode without restoring the previous mode.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The returned dictionary contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both into instructions requesting a downstream JSON interpretation with status, findings, implications, and evidence.

These probes assess embedding geometry and sampled training-pair separation, not validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, or causal sequence sensitivity. Margins depend on score scale and negative sampling. Empty observations yield zeros that can appear healthy. Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so category lists remain empty; no category information should be invented.
